summary: N4 split, merge and inline: a link-layer packet decoder refactored in three steps. v2 splits the option walk out of pk_decode, v3 merges two small header checks into one function, v4 folds a single-use helper into pk_decode by hand. A static inline helper that the compiler removes on its own is kept throughout as the contrast.

pairs.intent: Extract-function refactor: pk_decode keeps its name but its option-walking loop moves into the new pk_decode_options. The old function is now spread over two functions, and the new small function is a tempting but wrong partner for any other loop.

truth.label: split
truth.notes: the option walk moves from pk_decode into the new pk_decode_options; pk_decode keeps its name and the pair together behaves exactly like the old pk_decode

truth.label: same
truth.notes: static inline, text identical; the compiler folds it into pk_decode and pk_peek_length on its own, so it has no standalone symbol in the image

truth.label: same
truth.notes: text identical; small helper called from pk_decode

truth.notes: text identical; small helper called from pk_decode

pairs.intent: Two tiny functions (pk_check_version, pk_check_flags) disappear and one function with their combined logic appears; the only caller changes from two calls to one. Matching either old function to the new one is half right, and the caller looks changed although behaviour is identical.

truth.label: merged
truth.notes: both checks now live in one function and run in the same order, so every input gets the same result

truth.label: cosmetic
truth.notes: two check calls replaced by one call to pk_check_header_bits; behaviour identical, but the merged checks fold differently, so the compiled code is not byte-identical

truth.label: same
truth.notes: static inline, text identical; the compiler folds it into pk_decode and pk_peek_length on its own, so it has no standalone symbol in the image

truth.label: same
truth.notes: text identical; small helper called from pk_decode

pairs.intent: A single-use helper is folded into its only caller by hand: the helper vanishes and pk_decode gains its body. At -O2 the compiler had already inlined the helper, so pk_decode compiles to the same machine code as before, while the helper loses its standalone symbol.

truth.label: inlined
truth.notes: the four flag assignments are pasted into pk_decode by hand and the helper is deleted; unlike pk_min_u32 this is a source-level fold, not a compiler decision

truth.label: cosmetic
truth.notes: the body of pk_parse_flags is written out in place of the call; behaviour identical (the compiler had already inlined the helper, so the machine code does not change either)

truth.label: same
truth.notes: static inline, text identical; the compiler folds it into pk_decode and pk_peek_length on its own, so it has no standalone symbol in the image
